---
title: "CSIL design and pilot"
subtitle: "A cited reconstruction that keeps 1993, 1994, and 1995 from collapsing into one start year"
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Scope of this chapter
This page reconstructs what public sources now support about CSIL’s design and early public appearance. It uses one contemporaneous 1995 newspaper, a 2012 official chronology, later participant/organizational decks, and a 2008 ministry-commissioned review that does **not** pick a start year. Original 1993–95 Ministry of Health instruments remain [wanted](../sources/wanted-ministry-csil-pilot-records.qmd). This chapter does **not** choose a single founding year.
:::

## How this chapter uses evidence

Statements below are labelled as one of:

- **Documented (contemporaneous)** — taken from a 1993–95 source that was inspected
- **Later official reconstruction** — a later government or statutory-officer account
- **Attributed recollection** — a later named participant or organizational account
- **Interpretation** — inferred from those sources, and said to be so
- **Open question** — not settled by inspected evidence

Later “established” wording is not treated as a contemporaneous authorization. Different verbs (established, pilot, introduced, province-wide, new) are kept as the sources wrote them.

## Classification used here

Experiment 002 asked what 1993, 1994, and 1995 mean in the founding chronology and classified the public record as **PARTIAL STAGED CHRONOLOGY** (ChatGPT review: PASS). That conclusion is a research input, not a merged experiment file.

In substance:

- Later official wording assigns **different meanings** to 1994 (pilot / introduced) and 1995 (province-wide).
- A contemporaneous late-1995 source still calls CSIL **new/pilot** and does not independently confirm province-wide completion.
- **1993** appears only as a later “established” label that conflicts with the same speaker’s later “1994.”
- The 2008 program-review synthesis dates CSIL only to “the 1990's.”

This is not a settled three-stage founding story. It is the strongest pattern the public catalogue currently supports.

## What CSIL was said to be in late 1995

The only inspected **contemporaneous** public description in this catalogue is the [HEU *Guardian*, November/December 1995](../sources/1995-heu-guardian-novdec.qmd) (union newspaper scan; CSIL passage on page 9).

That feature, in a sidebar about a family using ministry home-support money, calls CSIL:

> a new program of the Community Support Branch of the Continuing Care Division called “Choice in Supports for Independent Living” or CSIL. Designed as a pilot program for people with disabilities who want to take more responsibility for managing their own care, the scheme allows non-profit societies to receive direct funding to hire caregivers for community-based care.

Further statements on that page, as recorded in the catalogue:

- Sally Hamilton “manages the program for the ministry.”
- Of “65,000 continuing care clients in the province, only 130 access CSIL funds.”
- The ministry expected CSIL employers “to pay within the unionized range, provide statutory benefits and keep a small cushion in the event of emergency.”

**Documented (contemporaneous):** by late 1995 a program publicly named Choice in Supports for Independent Living existed; HEU described it as new/pilot; HEU placed it in **Community Support Branch of the Continuing Care Division**, Ministry of Health; HEU described direct funding to non-profit societies to hire caregivers.

**What that source does not show.** It does not date the start to 1993, 1994, or 1995. It does not name ECPM, Creekview, Paul Gauthier, or a design committee. “Designed as a pilot” in a November/December 1995 newspaper can mean still piloting, recently piloted, or loosely “new.” HEU is a union newspaper with an interest in unionized home-support wages; treat cost and “pilot” wording as HEU’s contemporaneous report, not as a ministry instrument.

## Later official chronology: 1994 pilot / 1995 province-wide

[Ombudsperson, *The Best of Care* Part 2 (2012)](../sources/2012-ombudsperson-best-of-care.qmd) is a later official reconstruction, not a 1990s file. Volume 1 states:

> Seniors and their families can obtain funding from the government to hire and manage their own home support services, through the Choice in Supports for Independent Living Program, established as a pilot in 1994 and implemented province-wide in 1995.

The narrative paragraph repeats the pairing and adds that the new policy required regional health boards to fund self-managed home support “for people who had the ability to direct all aspects of their care or who had a client support group to do so on their behalf.”

Elsewhere the same volume says CSIL was “introduced in 1994” without repeating “pilot” in that sentence.

**Later official reconstruction:** 1994 = pilot / created / introduced; 1995 = province-wide implementation; the 1995-era policy (as later summarized) already contemplated either self-direction or a **client support group**.

**What that source does not show.** It does not quote the 1994 or 1995 instruments. It does not name Gauthier, ECPM, Creekview, Continuing Care Division, or Community Support Branch.

The contemporaneous HEU late-1995 “new/pilot” wording and the 2012 “province-wide in 1995” wording are **both kept**. They are not automatically the same event. Province-wide 1995 is **not** upgraded to a verified-inspected founding fact.

## Later “established” labels: 1993 and 1994

| Source | Type | Wording recorded in the catalogue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Gauthier 2014 SCI presentation](../sources/2014-gauthier-sci-csil-presentation.qmd) | Attributed recollection | “Established by the Ministry of Health in British Columbia in **1993**, with people with disabilities in the forefront of the program design.” Also: “The Pilot — 50 people tried it out.” Collaboration among home-support agencies, ministry senior staff, and consumers. |
| [Gauthier 2015 Module 1](../sources/2015-gauthier-csil-module-1.qmd) | Attributed recollection | Nearly the same sentence with **1994** instead of 1993. |
| [IFRC Our Team](../sources/ifrc-our-team.qmd) | Attributed recollection | Gauthier “started on the CSIL program in **1994**.” |

: Later start-year labels — not reconciled into one founding year

**1993** is not used in the inspected contemporaneous HEU piece or in the 2012 Ombudsperson chronology. It is a later “established” label from one 2014 deck, and it conflicts with the same speaker’s 2015 “1994.” This archive does **not** treat 1993 as a verified distinct stage (design approval versus pilot intake versus personal involvement).

**1994** is used both as later official “pilot / introduced” and as later recollection “established” / “started.” Those verbs are not synonyms here.

The [2008 CSIL Program Review Synthesis Report](../sources/2008-program-review-synthesis.qmd) (inspected Internet Archive Microlog fiche) dates participation “since its establishment in the 1990's” and does **not** choose 1993 versus 1994. It must not be used to pick a start year.

A secondary digest of *Hutchinson* ([2005 CanLIIDocs 513](../sources/2005-human-rights-digest-hutchinson.qmd)) says a client was accepted on CSIL in **1998**. That is only a terminus ante quem from a digest, not a founding date.

## Ministry records that remain missing

No original 1993–95 Ministry of Health design file, Treasury Board submission, Order in Council, pilot circular, or regional-board direction has been inspected. The [wanted class record](../sources/wanted-ministry-csil-pilot-records.qmd) remains copy-sought.

Still unknown without those files:

- which 1994 instrument (if any) the Ombudsperson treated as the “pilot”
- which 1995 act counted as “province-wide,” and how that relates to HEU’s late-1995 pilot wording and ~130-client snapshot
- what “established … in 1993” versus “1994” meant in later decks
- Sally Hamilton’s exact title and the instrument that created Community Support Branch CSIL
- whether “50 people tried it out” (Gauthier 2014) is contemporaneous or later recollection

A Roeher-cited October 1995 Ministry of **Social Services** individualized-funding / brokerage pilot (Kelly MacKinnon) is a **near-miss**. It is not treated as a Ministry of Health CSIL instrument.

## Documented roles (design / pilot period only)

| Person or body | What inspected evidence supports | What it does not support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ministry of Health, Community Support Branch / Continuing Care Division | HEU 1995 names this administrative home for a new/pilot CSIL program | The missing creating instrument |
| Sally Hamilton | HEU 1995: “manages the program for the ministry” | A recovered job description or signature on a 1990s file |
| Regional health boards | Ombudsperson 2012 later summary: required to fund self-managed home support after the province-wide policy | Contemporaneous 1995 board minutes |
| [Paul Gauthier](../people/paul-gauthier.qmd) | Later official honour: “Initiator” of CSIL ([Order of Canada citation](../sources/2023-order-of-canada-paul-gauthier.qmd)). Later IFRC/Gauthier decks: founder language; 1993 or 1994 “established”; 50-person pilot | A contemporaneous 1993–95 ministry appointment; inferred sole founder credit |
| [Joseph Theriault](../people/joseph-theriault.qmd) | Later IFRC wording: travelled with Gauthier to “create and promote” CSIL after ECPM | Any 1990s ministry title |
| Home-support agencies, ministry senior staff, and “consumers” | Gauthier 2014 later list of who was “initially involved” | Named committee membership |
| Creekview residents / [Walt Lawrence](../people/walt-lawrence.qmd) / [Doug Mowat](../people/doug-mowat.qmd) | No inspected 1993–95 source in this catalogue names them in CSIL design | Design-group membership (not inferred) |

: Documented and excluded roles for CSIL design and pilot

Formal design-group membership is **not** inferred for anyone from later founder language or from Creekview participation.

Relationship to ECPM is reserved to the [ECPM chapter](ecpm.qmd): later accounts name ECPM as a pre-CSIL step; no contemporaneous instrument inspected here proves formal succession.

## Unresolved questions

1. What each of 1993, 1994, and 1995 authorized, if they authorized different things.
2. How HEU’s late-1995 “non-profit societies” description relates to later individual-employer and client-support-group language (taken up on [Later evolution](evolution.qmd)).
3. Whether 1993–95 Hansard names CSIL (not retrieved for this chapter).
4. Whether a 50-person pilot is documented outside later Gauthier slides.
5. Who sat on any design, advisory, or working group, in what capacity, and in which year.

Those questions belong with [Issue #4](https://github.com/jordanforge-ca/csil-history/issues/4) and [Issue #6](https://github.com/jordanforge-ca/csil-history/issues/6). They are not resolved by picking a start year.
